sources.entry: Mole Widget - Lightweight system monitor with live CPU, memory, disk, network, battery, and process stats in a resizable desktop widget managed from the menu bar. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/bsnkhua/mole-widget) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Mole Widget is a lightweight, native Swift/SwiftUI macOS desktop widget that shows live CPU, memory, disk, network, battery and process stats, styled after the terminal output of the mole `mo status` CLI.
summary.what_it_does: The widget is a borderless window placed at desktop level, above the wallpaper and below application windows. It displays a header with chip, RAM, macOS version, uptime and a composite health score (0–100), plus sections for CPU (total usage, top-3 cores, load average, SoC temperature, sparkline), memory, disk (usage and read/write speed), power (charge, health, cycle count, temperature), network (download/upload sparklines, interface and local IP) and the top-3 processes by CPU. A usage history view keeps up to 12 hours of CPU and RAM data with a scrubber that shows the heaviest processes at a chosen moment. Menu bar items can show live CPU, memory and CPU temperature, and settings cover opacity, visible sections, refresh rate, font and launch at login. The window can be dragged, resized (490–880 pt), locked, or hidden, and these states are remembered across launches.
use_cases: monitor mac cpu and memory usage on the desktop
check battery health and cycle count on a macbook
watch network throughput and disk activity at a glance
see which processes are using the most resources over time
show system stats in the menu bar
keep a terminal-style system dashboard visible on the desktop
notable: Desktop-level borderless window that stays below regular windows, visible on all Spaces, and ignored by Mission Control and ⌘Tab
Usage History with 1h/4h/12h range and a scrubber showing heaviest processes at any moment
Menu bar metrics for CPU, memory and CPU temperature that stay live while the widget is hidden
Signed and notarized DMG, plus a Homebrew cask that defers updates to Sparkle
Pure-function computation over raw snapshots, with 80 unit tests
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and a Swift 6 toolchain for source builds
Tests must be run through make test, since a bare swift test silently runs zero tests on machines without full Xcode
Listed as freeware in the awesome-mac list; no license is named in the README
keywords: see what is using my mac
